Problem Statement

There is a tree with NNN vertices, numbered 1,2,…,N1, 2, \ldots, N1,2,…,N. For each iii (1≤i≤N−11 \leq i \leq N - 11≤i≤N−1), the iii-th edge connects Vertex xix_ixi​ and yiy_iyi​.

Taro has decided to paint each vertex in white or black, so that any black vertex can be reached from any other black vertex by passing through only black vertices.

You are given a positive integer MMM. For each vvv (1≤v≤N1 \leq v \leq N1≤v≤N), answer the following question:

  • Assuming that Vertex vvv has to be black, find the number of ways in which the vertices can be painted, modulo MMM.

Constraints

  • All values in input are integers.
  • 1≤N≤1051 \leq N \leq 10^51≤N≤105
  • 2≤M≤1092 \leq M \leq 10^92≤M≤109
  • 1≤xi,yi≤N1 \leq x_i, y_i \leq N1≤xi​,yi​≤N
  • The given graph is a tree.

Input

Input is given from Standard Input in the following format:

NNN MMM
x1x_1x1​ y1y_1y1​
x2x_2x2​ y2y_2y2​
:::
xN−1x_{N - 1}xN−1​ yN−1y_{N - 1}yN−1​

Output

Print NNN lines. The vvv-th (1≤v≤N1 \leq v \leq N1≤v≤N) line should contain the answer to the following question:

  • Assuming that Vertex vvv has to be black, find the number of ways in which the vertices can be painted, modulo MMM.
